I'll build this from current coaching, scheme, and beat-writer sources rather than recycled priors. Pulling NFC South and NFC West staff identities, personnel/coverage tendencies, and local reporting handles first.

Coaching identities and early-season personnel/PROE are in. Next I’m pulling coverage shells, pace, red-zone splits, and line/protection notes so the dossier isn’t just staff names.

One more pass on defensive-tendency and red-zone pages so the shell and finishing notes match the same Week 8 window as the personnel and pace boards.

Through Week 8 of the 2026 season (boards updated Nov. 3–6). This is a measured dossier, not a fabricated one. Where a requested split is not on an open board, it is marked **not published** rather than filled in.

**What is measured here:** coaching identity and play-caller, 11/12/13/21/22 rates, PROE and neutral pass rate, Sharp’s neutral play-clock (seconds of the 40-second clock used, not raw seconds between snaps), man/zone and middle-open/closed shells, blitz and box rates, positional yards per target, red-zone efficiency, and named beat writers.

**What is not on the open boards, so it is not invented:** exact Cover-0 / Cover-1 / Cover-2 / Cover-3 / Quarters / Cover-6 shares, stunt rate, simulated-creeper rate, slide-direction percentages, silent-count road false-start rates, individual corner or linebacker yards per route run and fantasy points per route, and pass rate when trailing by 8 or more versus leading by 8 or more. Middle-closed is the public proxy for single-high. Middle-open is the proxy for two-high. Script elasticity is inferred only from neutral pass rate versus overall pass rate, plus Sharp’s published “gear change” (trailing tempo versus neutral). Three public pace methodologies disagree on the raw second, so ranks are used instead of a false-precision seconds-per-play.

League anchors: neutral play-clock average 32.7 seconds used; neutral pass rate on the PROE board sits in the mid-50s; red-zone league TD rate 60%, pass rate 53%. [[1]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-team-pace-stats/) [[2]](https://muffed.ai/stats/pass-rate-over-expected) [[3]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-red-zone-stats/)

---

## NFC South

### Atlanta Falcons

**1. Scheme, personnel, PROE, pace, script**
- HC Kevin Stefanski (new). OC Tommy Rees calls the offense. DC Jeff Ulbrich, retained. [[4]](https://gridironexperts.com/nfl-coaches-list/)
- Identity: Kubiak wide-zone base (outside zone, counter, pin-and-pull, duo) with under-center play-action, plus Rees quick game, RPOs, and tempo only when the situation forces it. Early-down heavy sets and faster releases have been the stated fix for protection. [[5]](https://gridironexperts.com/kevin-stefanski-and-tommy-rees-impact-on-bijan-london-and-michael-penix-jr/) [[6]](https://www.thefalcoholic.com/atlanta-falcons-analysis/97825/methodical-falcons-deliver-a-new-winning-recipe)
- Personnel: 11 at 56%, 12 at 30%, 13 at 12%, 21 and 22 near zero. Two-tight-end rate 44%. [[7]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-offensive-personnel/)
- PROE −7.7, 29th. Neutral pass rate 46.9%. Overall pass rate 51.7%. They are a run script in neutral and only modestly more pass-heavy once the script breaks. That is low elasticity, not a full air-it-out trailing mode. [[2]](https://muffed.ai/stats/pass-rate-over-expected)
- Neutral play-clock 33.2 (20th, slower than average). No-huddle 5%. Gear change +2.0. [[1]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-team-pace-stats/)
- Exact trailing-by-8 versus leading-by-8 pass rates: **not published**.

**2. Protection**
- OL coach is Bill Callahan. Five-man rules, slide side, and silent-count road rates: **not published**. Tree prior is half-slide play-action, with the back or tight end checking the end the slide leaves. Do not treat that as a counted 2026 tendency.
- Early-season line grades were strong. The on-field answer to pressure has been heavier personnel and getting the ball out, which is a schematic tell that the five-man unit is not being asked to hold seven-step drops. [[6]](https://www.thefalcoholic.com/atlanta-falcons-analysis/97825/methodical-falcons-deliver-a-new-winning-recipe)
- Weakest 3-tech or wide-9 matchup: **not named on a public win-rate board** in this window. Do not assign a tackle or guard.

**3. Coverage and pressure**
- Man 22.3%, zone 70.5%, middle-closed 60.3%, middle-open 33.7%. Single-high lean, not a two-high team. [[8]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-coverage-schemes/)
- Blitz 21.8% (Sharp) / 25.0% (Muffed, 26th). Down from 35.2% and 2nd in 2025. Light box 40.8%, heavy box 31.4%, sub package 71%. [[9]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-defensive-tendencies/) [[10]](https://muffed.ai/stats/defense-blitz-rate/ATL)
- Shell-by-shell rates, stunt rate, creeper rate: **not published**.
- Leak is the boundary, not the slot. Yards per target: outside 9.4, slot 6.2, wide receiver 8.0, tight end 7.2, running back 4.3. [[11]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-coverage-stats-by-position/) Individual corner yards per route run: **not published**.

**4. Red zone and goal line**
- 22 trips, 64% TD (13th), 95% score, 5.50 points per trip, red-zone pass rate 48%. Goal-to-go TD 89%. Inside-the-10 TD 92%, best in the league. [[3]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-red-zone-stats/)
- Signature is Bijan Robinson, not a sneak package. Through Week 7 he had 46% of red-zone chances and 7 carries inside the 5. Penix’s red-zone share was 2%. [[12]](https://fantasyoutsiders.com/teams/atlanta-falcons)
- Tight-bunch rub rate and QB-sneak rate: **not published**.

**5. Beat writers**
- @marcraimondi (ESPN), @DOrlandoAJC (AJC), @Tori_McElhaney (team; Ulbrich used her for the Thursday Pearce pitch-count quote), @ZachKleinWSB. [[13]](https://www.readthebench.com/nfl-news-reporters-writers/) [[14]](https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2026/11/05/falcons-james-pearce-ulbrich/92625063007/)
- Wednesday is installation and the first injury report. Thursday is the participation window McElhaney and Raimondi actually move markets with. Friday is designation only. No stable coded “tell” beyond those windows should be assumed.

**6. Situational edges**
- Attack outside isolation and boundary go-routes against a single-high, low-blitz shell. Do not build the card around slot manufactured touches. Their slot number is fine.
- Close-game unders and opponent rush attempts are the structural bet: slow clock, −7.7 PROE, 12/13 personnel. Pass props on Atlanta only make sense after the lead is gone, and even then the overall-versus-neutral gap is small.
- James Pearce’s return is a Thursday pitch-count item, not a full-snap assumption, until McElhaney or Raimondi says otherwise. [[14]](https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2026/11/05/falcons-james-pearce-ulbrich/92625063007/)

---

### Carolina Panthers

**1. Scheme, personnel, PROE, pace, script**
- HC Dave Canales. OC Brad Idzik calls the offense. DC Ejiro Evero was fired Oct. 30. Todd Wash, the defensive line coach, is interim play-caller. Renaldo Hill still has the secondary. Almost the entire defensive sample below is Evero’s. Wash’s card can diverge immediately. [[4]](https://gridironexperts.com/nfl-coaches-list/) [[15]](https://bucswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/buccaneers/2026/11/04/nfc-south-coaching-changes-panthers-and-saints-fire-coaches/92608274007/)
- Offense is a quicker, spread-leaning Canales/Idzik script, not a heavy Shanahan personnel offense.
- Personnel: 11 at 59%, 12 at 29%, 13 at 12%, 21 and 22 essentially unused. [[7]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-offensive-personnel/)
- PROE +3.2, 4th. Neutral pass rate 64.0%. Overall pass rate 64.3%. This is the most inelastic pass script in the group. They throw whether the game is close or not. [[2]](https://muffed.ai/stats/pass-rate-over-expected)

[[11]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-coverage-stats-by-position/) Named nickel yards per route run: **not published**.

**4. Red zone and goal line**
- Best red-zone offense in the league: 23 trips, 87% TD, 100% score rate, 6.35 points per trip, +0.51 EPA per play. Red-zone pass rate 53%. Goal-to-go TD 93%. Inside-the-10 TD 88%. Zero turnovers. [[3]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-red-zone-stats/)
- Pro Football Reference split: 70 red-zone plays, 36 rushes and 34 pass attempts. Inside the 10: 20 rushes and 19 pass attempts. It is balanced, not a sneak package and not a fade package. [[37]](https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2026_splits.htm)
- George Kittle has 11 red-zone targets, 31% share. [[31]](https://fantasytools.ai/red-zone-stats/)
- Structural signature is 21 personnel and the fullback, with Kittle as the scoring target. Counted sneak rate and bunch-rub rate: **not published**.

**5. Beat writers**
- @LombardiHimself (David Lombardi, SF Standard; he posts the actual blitz-rate changes), @VicTafur, @Eric_Branch, @CamInman, Matt Maiocco at NBC Sports Bay Area. [[35]](https://x.com/LombardiHimself/status/2115588237540643019) [[26]](https://fiddlespicks.substack.com/p/list-of-beat-writers-for-every-nfl)
- Lombardi is the scheme-window feed, not just the injury feed. Wednesday–Friday value is skill-position participation (Kittle, the fullback, the tackles) and any Morris pressure quote. A Thursday “blitz is up again” note from Lombardi is more useful than a national preview.

**6. Situational edges**
- Slot crossers and bunch rubs against an 82% zone, middle-closed shell. Do not attack the tight end in coverage. 5.5 yards per target is a wall. Do not assume the boundary is soft. It is not.
- Colby versus a 3-tech is the protection matchup with a published scar. Williams is not the side to build a pressure prop on.
- Red-zone finishing is the strongest structural edge in this eight-team set. A 49ers red-zone trip has converted to a touchdown 87% of the time, on a balanced run/pass split. Fading that trip is fading the best number on the board.
- Pace will not save an over. Two percent no-huddle and a sticky pass rate mean points come from efficiency, not from extra snaps.

---

### Seattle Seahawks

**1. Scheme, personnel, PROE, pace, script**
- HC Mike Macdonald. OC Brian Fleury, new, from the 49ers’ tight end and run-game chair. DC Aden Durde. [[4]](https://gridironexperts.com/nfl-coaches-list/) [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_NFL_offensive_coordinators)
- Personnel still carries the heavy, two-back look Fleury comes from: 11 at 47%, 12 at 26%, 13 at 5%, 21 at 14%, 22 at 8%. Two-back rate 22%, second only to San Francisco in this set. [[7]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-offensive-personnel/)
- PROE −5.2, 26th. Neutral pass rate 51.5%. Overall pass rate 55.7%. Modest pass bump once the script leaves neutral. Not a sudden air raid. [[2]](https://muffed.ai/stats/pass-rate-over-expected)
- Slow. Sharp neutral play-clock 33.3 (22nd). Muffed’s different seconds-between-snaps metric has them 29th at 31.63. No-huddle 3%. Gear change +0.7. Rank order is the point: they are in the slow cluster either way. [[1]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-team-pace-stats/) [[38]](https://muffed.ai/stats/team-pace/SEA)
- Trailing-by-8 versus leading-by-8: **not published**.

**2. Protection**
- PFF’s cited five: Charles Cross, Grey Zabel, Jalen Sundell, Quenton Nelson, Abraham Lucas. Nelson’s first game showed up as a run blocker. The same note flagged the guard pairing after Zabel’s move. The table in that piece lists Nelson at right guard and Zabel at left guard. The prose flags the guard spot, not the tackles. [[24]](https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-offensive-line-rankings-2026)
- Versus a 3-tech, the guard pairing is the published concern. Versus a wide-9, Cross and Lucas are the strength side when both are healthy. Slide direction: **not published**, so do not assign which tackle is left alone.
- Silent-count road rate: **not published**. Low no-huddle and a slow clock mean low cadence exposure until a two-minute deficit.

**3. Coverage and pressure**
- Man 4.6%, the lowest man rate in the league. Zone 76.9%. Middle-open 53.0%, middle-closed 32.3%. This is a zone, two-high-capable coverage defense. [[8]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-coverage-schemes/)
- Blitz 21.1%, among the lowest in the league. Light box 48.8%, heavy box 17.7%, sub package 88% (highest of these eight). They do not need a fifth rusher, and they do not play base. [[9]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-defensive-tendencies/)
- Stunt and creeper rates: **not published**. The counted story is four-man rush, five or six defensive backs, almost no man.
- There is no slot weak link. Slot yards per target 3.9 is the best number on the entire 32-team board in this window. Wide receiver 6.1, tight end 5.6, back 5.1. The only relative window is outside at 7.8, and that is still not a leak by league standards. [[11]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-coverage-stats-by-position/)
- Individual corner yards per route run: **not published**, and the team splits say you should not go hunting for one in the slot.

**4. Red zone and goal line**
- Offense: 26 trips, 50% TD (27th), red-zone pass rate 51%, goal-to-go TD 58%, inside-the-10 TD 53%. They do not finish. [[3]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-red-zone-stats/)
- Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 13 red-zone targets, a 35% share. Target volume has not become touchdown efficiency. [[31]](https://fantasytools.ai/red-zone-stats/)
- Defense: Sharp’s red-zone defensive board lists Seattle last in the league. That is the outlier. The between-the-20s coverage is elite. The red zone is not. [[3]](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/stats-nfl/nfl-red-zone-stats/)
- Sneak rate and bunch-rub rate: **not published**.

**5. Beat writers**
- @bcondotta (Bob Condotta, Seattle Times; he files the postgame grades and the availability), @gbellseattle, @dannyoneil. [[39]](https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/) [[13]](https://www.readthebench.com/nfl-news-reporters-writers/)
- The live Wednesday–Friday market is quarterback availability. Condotta’s desk has been on Darnold’s absence and Drew Lock’s relief work. A Thursday limited or a Friday out designation changes the entire offensive card, because Fleury’s slow, low-PROE script has even less margin without the starter. Do not treat a beat-writer “he looked good in individual drills” line as a full-practice clearance.

**6. Situational edges**
- Do not bet slot receivers, option routes, or manufactured slot touches against this defense. 3.9 yards per target is the worst number on the board to attack.
- The coverage window, if you need one between the 20s, is outside isolation against a two-high zone that almost never plays man. It is a relative window, not a collapse.
- The real defensive soft spot is the red zone. Sharp has them last in red-zone defense while they are first-tier in yards per target everywhere else. Inside-the-10 and goal-line props against Seattle have a structural case that slot props do not.
- Their own offense is slow, PROE-negative, and 50% in the red zone. Close-game unders and opponent red-zone stops against Seattle’s offense are the offensive side of the same card. A quarterback change, per Condotta’s window, makes that lean stronger, not weaker.

---

## How to use the eight cards together

| Team | Call sheet | Neutral identity | Defense to attack | Defense not to attack |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Atlanta | Rees / Ulbrich | Run, slow, low elasticity | Boundary vs single-high | Slot |
| Carolina | Idzik / Wash (sample is still Evero) | Pass, fast, inelastic | Boundary vs zone-blitz | Slot, and any prop that assumes Evero is still calling it |
| New Orleans | Moore / Staley | 11 personnel, fastest clock, no extra gear | Slot, linebacker zones, RB checkdowns, opponent red-zone runs | Treating them as a heavy personnel team |
| Tampa Bay | Robinson / Bowles | Extreme run when close or leading | Hot routes vs 40% blitz | “Soft corners,” and Bucs pass props in a lead |
| Arizona | LaFleur / Rallis | Balanced in neutral, passes when the script breaks | Outside and tight end vs two-high | Slot, and Arizona red-zone TD rate |
| Rams | McVay / Shula | 13 to manage, no-huddle 11 to throw | Small slot case only | Tight end, and a full-game pass total that ignores personnel |
| San Francisco | Shanahan / Morris | 21 personnel, pass rate stuck near 53%, best red zone | Slot vs zone | Tight end coverage, Williams in protection, fading their red-zone trip |
| Seattle | Fleury / Durde | Heavy, slow, low PROE, worst red-zone defense | Inside the 10, outside only as a relative window | Slot, anything that needs man coverage |

Three rules that survive the missing splits:

1. If the number is a team yards-per-target split or a PROE rank, it is usable. If it is a slide percentage, a creeper rate, a sneak rate, or a named corner’s yards per route run, it was not on the open board and it is not in this dossier.
2. Coordinator changes break the card. Carolina’s blitz and zone rates are mostly Evero’s. Seattle’s offensive card is Fleury’s, not last year’s Kubiak card. Morris’s blitz rate is already up from Saleh’s. Price the man who has the headset this week.
3. Wednesday install, Thursday participation, Friday designation. The handles above are the feeds that move those windows. A quote about effort is not a tell. A participation line, a pitch count, or a “he is still calling it” line is.

waves.title: Where No Human or Machine Has Gone: Neuro-Visuomotor Saccades, Proprioceptive Brace Penalty, Thermal Cramping & Circadian NFL Alpha
waves.content:
**1. Quarterback Visuomotor Saccade Latency & Peripheral Field-of-View Occlusion**

Quarterbacks execute rapid foveal saccades to shift gaze between defensive players (e.g., post-snap rotating safety from middle-of-field open to closed alignments) while the pocket collapses, requiring head rotation. Typical saccadic reaction time (latency from target appearance to movement onset) is approximately 215 ms in humans, with sensory-to-motor delays of ~80 ms plus central processing.[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/chapter/bookseries/abs/pii/S0079612321002156)[[2]](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/screen-play/202504/how-processing-speed-makes-a-good-quarterback-great) Athletes, including those in open-skill sports, often exhibit faster latencies and higher rates of express saccades than non-athletes.[[3]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383217817_Saccade_Latency_and_Metrics_in_the_Interleaved_Pro-_and_Anti-Saccade_Task_in_Open_Skill_Sports_Athletes)

The model integrates:
- Fixed latency + amplitude-dependent travel/processing time.
- Vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) stabilization during head rotation (gain typically 0.9–1.0; compensatory eye movement opposes head velocity ω to maintain gaze).[[4]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/vestibulo-ocular-reflex)[[5]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380685374_Dynamic_Visual_Acuity_Vestibulo-Ocular_Reflex_and_Visual_Field_in_National_Football_League_NFL_Officiating_Physiology_and_Visualization_Engineering_for_3D_Virtual_On-Field_Training)
- Peripheral occlusion from facemask/visor (typically 15–30° temporal/inferior blockage, forcing extra head turns or saccades into occluded zones).

**Closed-form equations:**

Total visuomotor latency per read shift (seconds):

\[ L_{vm}(\theta, \omega, \alpha) = L_{base} + k \cdot \theta + t_{VOR}(\omega) \cdot (1 - G_{VOR}) + p_{occ}(\alpha) \]

Where:
- \( L_{base} \): base latency (~0.200–0.215 s).
- \( k \): travel/processing coefficient (~0.001–0.002 s/deg; yields 200–240 ms total for 30° per the query).
- \( \theta \): angular read shift (deg, e.g., 30°).
- \( t_{VOR}(\omega) = \tau_{VOR} \cdot (1 - e^{-\omega / \omega_0}) \): stabilization delay under head angular velocity ω (rad/s) during pocket spin/compression; τ_VOR ≈ 0.015–0.050 s, ω₀ normalization constant (~2–5 rad/s).
- \( G_{VOR} \): VOR gain (0.85–0.98 under helmet constraints).
- \( p_{occ}(\alpha) = m \cdot \max(0, \alpha - \alpha_{free}) \): occlusion penalty (s); m ≈ 0.003–0.008 s/deg occluded; α = occlusion angle (facemask/visor, typically 20°); α_free = unobstructed peripheral field threshold (~15–25°).

For multiple sequential reads (n shifts) under continuous rotation:

\[ L_{total} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} L_{vm}(\theta_i, \omega_i, \alpha) + t_{proc} \cdot (n-1) \]

Effective peripheral field-of-view is reduced: FOV_eff = FOV_base − α − f(helmet tilt). This increases n or forces slower head-turn saccades. Under interior pocket compression, ω > 1–3 rad/s elevates t_VOR, adding 20–60 ms per major shift. Total decision-release window under 2.5–3.0 s must accommodate 3–5 reads, leaving <500 ms for mechanics.[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/RK-5ADphyCM)

**Parameter Table 1:**

Parameter | Symbol | Value Range | Units | Notes
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Base saccade latency | L_base | 0.200–0.215 | s | Typical; athletes faster[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/chapter/bookseries/abs/pii/S0079612321002156)[[3]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383217817_Saccade_Latency_and_Metrics_in_the_Interleaved_Pro-_and_Anti-Saccade_Task_in_Open_Skill_Sports_Athletes)
Travel coeff. per 30° | k·30 | 0.200–0.240 | s | Query-specified bundled time
VOR time constant | τ_VOR | 0.015–0.050 | s | Stabilization under rotation
VOR gain | G_VOR | 0.85–0.98 | unitless | Helmet/facemask reduces from ideal ~1.0
Occlusion angle (facemask/visor) | α | 15–30 | deg | Temporal/inferior blockage
Occlusion penalty coeff. | m | 0.003–0.008 | s/deg | Extra saccades/head turns
Head rotation rate (compressed pocket) | ω | 1–4 | rad/s | MOFO-to-MOFC spin transition

**2. Ankle/Knee Spat-Tape & Rigid-Hinge Brace Proprioceptive Force-Transduction Penalty**

Heavy prophylactic spatting (tape) or rigid-hinge braces restrict talocrural dorsiflexion range-of-motion (ROM), reduce Achilles tendon elastic strain-energy storage/recovery, and alter proprioceptive feedback. Studies show taping reduces peak dorsiflexion angle, can increase ground-reaction force (GRF) loading rates (4–18%), and impairs rate of force development or jump height.[[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1440244024002263)[[8]](https://journals.lww.com/nsca-jscr/fulltext/2014/05000/the_effect_of_ankle_taping_on_the_ground_reaction.30.aspx) Meta-analyses indicate limited overall effects on GRF or inversion in many tasks but clear ROM restriction.[[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1440244022000421)

**Closed-form mechanical model:**

Reduced dorsiflexion: θ_df,tape = θ_df,natural · (1 − r), where r = restriction factor (0.15–0.35 for heavy spat + hinge).

Achilles tendon displacement x ≈ r_tendon · θ_df (r_tendon ≈ 0.05–0.06 m effective moment arm).

Elastic strain energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k_{tendon} x^2 \) (k_tendon ≈ 150–250 N/mm typical).

Peak ground-reaction impulse penalty:

\[ J_{reduced} = J_0 \cdot \left(1 - \beta \cdot \frac{E_{reduced}}{E_0}\right) \]

β = transduction efficiency penalty (0.04–0.07 per query; incorporates proprioceptive dampening and altered force-velocity curve).

3-cone cut velocity penalty (derived from power output ∝ √E):

\[ v_{cut,reduced} = v_0 \cdot \sqrt{1 - \beta \cdot \frac{E_{reduced}}{E_0}} \approx v_0 \cdot (1 - 0.5\beta \cdot \frac{\Delta E}{E_0}) \]

For heavy spat + rigid hinge, net −4% to −7% on peak impulse and cut velocity is consistent with observed reductions in explosive change-of-direction. Stiffer tape increases early loading rate but reduces late-stance energy return.

**Parameter Table 2:**

Parameter | Value (Natural) | Value (Taped/Braced) | Penalty | Units | Notes
--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Dorsiflexion ROM (θ_df) | 20–25 | 12–18 | 15–35% reduction | deg | Primary mechanical limit
Achilles energy storage (E) | 30–45 | 20–35 | −20–35% | J | Per push-off
Peak GR impulse (J) | baseline | — | −4 to −7% | % | Query range; rate of force development hit harder
3-cone cut velocity | baseline | — | −4 to −7% | % | Explosive cut metric
Tape/brace stiffness multiplier | 1.0 | 1.8–3.0 | — | unitless | Increases effective k_ankle

**3. Core Hyperthermia (>39.2°C) & Sweat-Electrolyte Sodium Depletion Cramping Hazard in 310+ lb Linemen**

Large linemen (>310 lb / ~140 kg) have high metabolic heat production (M), lower surface-area-to-mass ratio, and high sweat rates, elevating exertional heat stroke risk. They comprise the majority of football EHS cases.[[10]](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/19417381261486272?url_ver=Z39.88-2003&rfr_id=ori:rid:crossref.org&rfr_dat=cr_pub%20%200pubmed) Core temperature >39.2°C combined with sodium losses (>5 g projected per practice) drives neuromuscular failure, cramping, pass-rush win-rate collapse, and missed-tackle spikes in Q3/Q4. WBGT >28°C markedly increases risk.[[11]](https://journals.lww.com/acsm-msse/fulltext/2007/03000/exertional_heat_illness_during_training_and.20.aspx)[[12]](https://www.uptodate.com/contents/exertional-heat-illness-in-adolescents-and-adults-epidemiology-thermoregulation-risk-factors-and-diagnosis/print) Cramp-prone players show ~2× higher sweat sodium concentration (~50–55 mmol/L).[[13]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238249063_SWEAT_AND_SODIUM_LOSSES_IN_CRAMP-PRONE_PROFESSIONAL_FOOTBALL_PLAYERS)

**Heat-storage differential equation (humid stadiums vs. domes):**

\[ m \cdot c_p \cdot \frac{dT_{core}}{dt} = M_{net} + H_{env}(WBGT) - E_{max} - (R + C + K) \]

Where m = body mass (140 kg), c_p ≈ 0.83 kcal/kg/°C (3.47 kJ/kg/°C), M_net = metabolic rate minus external work (high for linemen: 800–1200 W), H_env scales with WBGT (0.7·wet-bulb dominant in humid MIA/TB/JAX visitor sideline sun exposure), E_max = evaporative cooling (severely limited when relative humidity >70–80%; near zero in full pads), R+C+K = radiative/convective/conductive terms (negative in sun-exposed heat).

Closed-form solution assuming quasi-constant load (simplified exponential approach to equilibrium):

\[ T_{core}(t) = T_0 + \Delta T_{ss} \left(1 - e^{-t/\tau}\right) \]

ΔT_ss = (M_net + H_env − E_max) / (m·c_p·λ), τ = time constant (~30–60 min for linemen in pads; shorter in humidity). Time-to-39.2°C ≈ 35–55 min at WBGT 30–32°C (outdoor humid) vs. >90 min in climate-controlled domes (effective WBGT <20°C with AC).

Sodium depletion: Na_loss(t) = [Na]_sweat · sweat_rate · t (sweat_rate 2.5–4.0 L/h for 140 kg linemen; [Na]_sweat 25–60 mmol/L, higher in cramp-prone). Threshold for cramping hazard ~150–250 mmol cumulative deficit + T_core >39.2°C.

Q3/Q4 performance collapse modeled as win-rate multiplier w = 1 − γ·(T_core − 39.2) − δ·(Na_deficit / threshold), γ≈0.15–0.25 per °C, δ≈0.10–0.20 per unit normalized deficit. Outdoor humid venues accelerate onset by 1.5–2× vs. domes.

**Parameter Table 3:**

Parameter | Value (310+ lb Lineman) | Units | Notes
--- | --- | --- | ---
Body mass (m) | 140–160 | kg | Typical defensive/offensive lineman
Specific heat (c_p) | 3.47 | kJ/kg/°C | Standard
Metabolic heat (M_net, game) | 800–1400 | W | Position-specific, pads increase
Critical WBGT | >28 | °C | High risk threshold[[11]](https://journals.lww.com/acsm-msse/fulltext/2007/03000/exertional_heat_illness_during_training_and.20.aspx)
Sweat rate | 2.5–4.0 | L/h | Humid heat + mass
Sweat [Na+] (cramp-prone) | 50–60 | mmol/L | ~2× non-crampers[[13]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238249063_SWEAT_AND_SODIUM_LOSSES_IN_CRAMP-PRONE_PROFESSIONAL_FOOTBALL_PLAYERS)
Time-to-39.2°C (humid outdoor) | 35–55 | min | Q3/Q4 onset driver
Dome advantage | +40–60 | min delay | Reduced H_env

**4. Circadian Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN) Phase Shift, Cortisol Awakening Response, and Neuromuscular Reaction-Time Latency**

The SCN master clock entrains to local light/dark cycles; 3-hour coast difference produces misalignment. Peak athletic performance occurs in late afternoon/early evening on endogenous clock. West-coast teams playing 1:00 PM ET games operate at ~10:00 AM body time (post-awakening but pre-peak), while East-coast teams in late MNF/SNF/TNF road games face misalignment in the opposing direction.[[14]](https://aasm.org/circadian-timing-may-give-edge-to-west-coast-nfl-teams-in-night-games/)[[15]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3825451/) Historical data show West-coast advantage in night games against East-coast opponents after adjusting for quality.[[15]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3825451/)

**Performance model:**

Reaction time latency:

\[ RT(t_{body}) = RT_0 \left[1 + a \cdot \left|\sin\left(\frac{2\pi (t_{body} - t_{peak})}{24}\right)\right| + b \cdot | \Delta \phi | + c \cdot (1 - CAR_{norm}) \right] \]

- t_body = local clock time adjusted by time-zone shift (Δφ = ±3 h).
- t_peak ≈ 16–18 h (4–6 PM body time).
- a ≈ 0.05–0.12 (circadian amplitude).
- b ≈ 0.02–0.04 per hour misalignment.
- CAR_norm = normalized cortisol awakening response (peaks ~30 min post-waking; blunted if game requires very early wake for travel or early kickoff). Early body-clock games suppress CAR, elevating RT by 10–25 ms.
- Neuromuscular penalty compounds with travel fatigue.

For West-coast at 1 PM ET (10 AM body): near CAR tail but far from peak → +8–15% RT latency vs. optimal. East-coast late window on road: closer to or past peak but accumulated fatigue. Closed-form phase shift: effective performance decrement (%) ≈ 3–6% per hour deviation from t_peak in first 48 h post-travel.

**Parameter Table 4:**

Parameter | Value | Units | Notes
--- | --- | --- | ---
Time-zone shift (coast difference) | 3 | h | SCN entrainment lag
Circadian peak (t_peak) | 16–18 | h body time | Late afternoon optimum
RT base (optimal) | 180–220 | ms | Neuromuscular
Amplitude (a) | 0.05–0.12 | unitless | Sinusoidal modulation
Misalignment coeff. (b) | 0.02–0.04 | per h | Includes SCN desynchrony
CAR suppression penalty | 0.05–0.10 | unitless | Blunted morning response for early games
West 1 PM ET effective time | 10 AM body | — | Suboptimal arousal window
East late road (e.g. 8:20 PM ET) | ~5 PM body | — | Closer to peak but fatigue accumulates

These integrated models combine established physiological constants with NFL-specific constraints to quantify performance decrements. They enable predictive simulation of play-by-play biomechanical efficiency, heat-induced collapse probability, and schedule-dependent reaction-time distributions for medical, training, and strategic optimization. Parameters can be refined with player-specific telemetry.

waves.title: Where No Human or Machine Has Gone: Cross-Derivative Internal Bookmaker Contradiction Arbitrage Across All 77+ NFL Market Types
waves.content:
**The framework enforces global consistency across siloed marginals by mapping every de-vigged offer to linear (and selected inequality) constraints derived from the physical identities of an NFL game.** A single game generates roughly 1,800 offers (main lines, quarters, halves, player props, alternate ladders, specials, anytime TD, kicking, script, clock). Each offer is converted to a de-vigged implied expectation or probability π_k. The vector π ∈ ℝ^K (K ≈ 400–600 after aggregation) must lie in the marginal-consistency polytope defined by conservation equalities and Fréchet–Hoeffding-type inequalities on joints and sums. Violations are detected via linear programming feasibility; the most mispriced leg is isolated via Bregman (KL) projection leave-one-out or dual sensitivity.[[1]](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/1606.02825)[[2]](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1606.02825)

### De-vigging
For American odds o:
- Favorite (−110): raw prob = 110 / (110 + 100) = 0.5238.
- Underdog (+100): raw prob = 100 / 200 = 0.5000.
- Normalize two-way markets so probabilities sum to 1. For multi-outcome or ladders, solve the power method or use Shin’s method to extract no-vig probabilities. Alternate lines supply multiple points on the implied CDF, allowing extraction of both mean and limited higher moments. Convert O/U lines to implied expectations via normal or skewed-T approximation when full ladders are unavailable. The resulting π_market is the observed point that may lie outside the feasible polytope.

### Conservation Constraints
All identities are expressed as linear equalities Aπ = b (exact accounting) and inequalities Cπ ≤ d (probabilistic bounds, zero-sum shares, leakage, Fréchet–Hoeffding copula bounds on joint tail probabilities, non-negativity, and script elasticities). The polytope is P = {π | Aπ = b, Cπ ≤ d, l ≤ π ≤ u}.

**(1) Team Scoring Identity**  
Let π contain: E[T_full], E[T_1Q], E[T_2Q], E[T_3Q], E[T_4Q], E[T_1H], E[T_2H], E[TD_off], E[FG], E[PAT], E[XP2], E[safety], E[DST_TD], E[Kick_pts], {P_i = de-vigged prob player i scores ≥1 TD for i=1…N}, P_DST_TD.  

Equality rows in Aπ = b:
- E[T_full] − (E[T_1Q] + E[T_2Q] + E[T_3Q] + E[T_4Q]) = 0
- E[T_full] − (E[T_1H] + E[T_2H]) = 0
- E[T_full] − (6·E[TD_off] + 3·E[FG] + E[PAT] + 2·E[XP2] + 2·E[safety] + 6·E[DST_TD]) = 0
- E[Kick_pts] − (3·E[FG] + E[PAT] + 2·E[XP2]) = 0
- E[TD_off] − (∑ P_i + P_DST_TD) = 0 (approximate; multiples are rare)

Inequality rows in Cπ ≤ d (Fréchet-style):
- ∑ P_i ≥ E[TD_off] (lower Fréchet)
- ∑ P_i ≤ E[TD_off] + 0.25·E[TD_off] (upper accounting for multiples and D/ST overlap)
- All expectations ≥ 0 and ≤ realistic maxima (e.g., E[T_full] ≤ 62, E[FG] ≤ 5).

- E[PA] − E[PC] − E[incompletes] − E[sacks] ≈ 0 (incompletes inferred or bounded)

These translate to linear inequalities on second-moment marginals extracted from ladder spreads. Fréchet–Hoeffding bounds on joint reception/yardage tails add further Cπ ≤ d rows (e.g., P(R1 > a, RY_total > b) bounds given marginal CDFs).

### No-Arbitrage Polytope and Farkas Lemma
The feasible set P is a convex polytope. Market π_market is inconsistent if π_market ∉ P. Feasibility is checked by LP:

min 0  
s.t. Aπ = b  
Cπ ≤ d  
l ≤ π ≤ u

If infeasible, Farkas’ lemma supplies a certificate. There exist dual multipliers y (unrestricted, for equalities) and z ≥ 0 (for inequalities) such that:

yᵀ A + zᵀ C = 0  
yᵀ b + zᵀ d < 0

(with appropriate adjustment for the bound constraints). The vector (y, z) identifies the linear combination of constraints that produces a contradiction; its magnitude on individual legs ranks structural tension. In betting terms, it corresponds to a synthetic “portfolio” of prop legs whose implied expectations cannot simultaneously hold.

### Bregman / KL Projection onto the Polytope
To incorporate a prior π₀ (constructed from a play-by-play Monte Carlo engine that enforces all conservations by design—drive simulation, Dirichlet target allocation, script-dependent play calling, consistent stat accumulation), solve the Bregman projection:

min_π D_R(π ‖ π₀)  
s.t. Aπ = b, Cπ ≤ d, l ≤ π ≤ u

where D_R is the Bregman divergence generated by a strictly convex R. For probability-like coordinates, negative entropy R(π) = ∑ π_i ln π_i yields Kullback–Leibler divergence KL(π ‖ π₀). For general expectations, quadratic or other separable convex functions can be used; the geometry remains Bregman. This projection can be solved via Frank–Wolfe (conditional gradient) with a linear optimization oracle over P, or by interior-point/barrier methods in modern solvers.[[1]](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/1606.02825)

The projected π* is the “closest” consistent set of marginals. Lagrange multipliers λ associated with each market-derived constraint measure tension. Largest |λ_k| flags the most violated marginal.

### Ranking the Single Most Mispriced Leg
**Algorithm (leave-one-out Bregman projection):**
1. Construct full constraint system (A, b, C, d) from all 1,800 offers.
2. For each leg k = 1 to K:
   - Form reduced system (A⁻ᵏ, b⁻ᵏ, C⁻ᵏ, d⁻ᵏ) by removing all rows tied exclusively to offer k.
   - Compute π*⁻ᵏ = arg min D_R(π ‖ π₀) s.t. reduced constraints.
   - Compute mispricing score_k = |π*⁻ᵏ[k] − π_market[k]| / σ_k + λ_k² (normalized deviation plus squared dual from full projection).
3. Rank legs by descending score_k. The top leg is the single most mispriced derivative on the board—the one whose removal most relaxes the polytope tension.

import cvxpy as cp
import numpy as np

def build_constraints(offers, conservations):
    # offers: dict of de-vigged expectations/probs
    # conservations: list of (A_rows, b, C_rows, d) for each identity block
    A, b, C, d, l, u = aggregate_blocks(conservations, offers)
    return A, b, C, d, l, u

def project(A, b, C, d, l, u, pi0, divergence="KL"):
    n = len(pi0)
    pi = cp.Variable(n)
    if divergence == "KL":
        objective = cp.sum(pi * cp.log(pi / pi0))  # Bregman form
    else:
        objective = cp.sum_squares(pi - pi0)  # quadratic fallback
    prob = cp.Problem(cp.Minimize(objective),
                      [A @ pi == b, C @ pi <= d, pi >= l, pi <= u])
    prob.solve(solver=cp.GUROBI)  # or MOSEK, SCS
    return pi.value, prob.constraints  # return duals too

def rank_mispriced(offers, pi0):
    A, b, C, d, l, u = build_constraints(offers, [scoring_id, pass_rec_id, rush_clock_id])
    scores = []
    full_pi_star, duals = project(A, b, C, d, l, u, pi0)
    for k in range(len(offers)):
        A_red, b_red, C_red, d_red, l_red, u_red = remove_leg_constraints(A, b, C, d, l, u, k)
        pi_star_red = project(A_red, b_red, C_red, d_red, l_red, u_red, pi0)[0]
        deviation = abs(pi_star_red[k] - offers[k].implied)
        tension = abs(duals[k]) ** 2 if k < len(duals) else 0
        scores.append((offers[k].name, deviation + tension))
    scores.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
    return scores[0]  # single most mispriced leg
